title: D-limonene response in Fusarium proliferatum: a published-table audit
question: Which metabolic and signaling responses to terpene exposure are reproducible, and which depend on cellular context or a specific target?

sources.title: Zhou et al., D-limonene and histone acetylation in Fusarium proliferatum (2025)

claims.text: The source study compares three Fusarium proliferatum hyphal cultures exposed to 200 mM D-limonene for 24 hours with three untreated controls. The article reports substantial growth inhibition at this dose.
claims.limitation: Growth inhibition can cause secondary transcriptional and chromatin effects; the exposure differs greatly from the Penicillium biotransformation study.

claims.text: Publisher Table S3 lists three untreated and three D-limonene RNA-seq libraries; its reported mapped fractions range from 0.9013 to 0.9422.
claims.limitation: This checks the published QC summary, not reads, alignments, contamination, or batch structure.

claims.text: Publisher Table S4 contains 2,375 unique feature rows: 1,240 down and 1,135 up. All printed rows have adjusted p < 0.05 and absolute log2 fold change at least 1.
claims.limitation: These are author-computed statistics; the notebook does not re-estimate a count model or verify the stated feature universe.

claims.text: The article reports 1,134 upregulated genes, while Table S4 has 1,135 upregulated features. The extra up entry is rrna13; 1,134 up entries have FPRO_ identifiers, but four down entries also have rrna identifiers, so a uniform exclusion rule is not documented.
claims.limitation: The reason for the one-row mismatch remains unresolved; it should not be silently corrected.

claims.text: At adjusted p < 0.05, Table S5 has one H3K9ac-associated KEGG term, ribosome (ko03010), and no H3K27ac-associated KEGG terms.
claims.limitation: This is a within-study pathway-list audit, not a mediation analysis or proof that histone acetylation causes the RNA response.

claims.text: The article reports reduced H3K9ac and H3K27ac after D-limonene exposure and interprets transcriptome and ChIP-seq results as affecting translation and metabolism.
claims.limitation: Observed chromatin changes and expression associations do not establish direct limonene binding to a histone regulator.

claims.text: Reprocess the six PRJNA1234870 RNA-seq libraries against a pinned F. proliferatum reference, audit sample assignment and count-model assumptions, and check whether the one-row feature discrepancy persists.
claims.limitation: Raw-read reanalysis has not been run in this project.

claims.text: Compare D-limonene responses with the independent R-(+)-limonene Penicillium cohort only after confirming chemical stereochemistry, viability, dose, time, growth medium, and orthology mappings; test any nominated target with direct biochemical or chemical-genetic evidence.
claims.limitation: The present studies differ in organism, experimental goal, dose, and time and do not yet meet a replication criterion.
